messages.content: I have revised quotes for the Elizabeth Pointe and the Omni, but they are presenting the money differently. Can you put them on equal footing for one room, two adults, September 12 through 18?

Yes. Send me each quote's room charge, taxes, mandatory fees, parking, deposits, cancellation terms, and exact room-category wording. I will separate costs that count toward the stay from refundable holds.

Elizabeth Pointe says High Floor King, Private Balcony, Partial Ocean View. The six-night room charge is $2,514. Breakfast is included. Taxes are $301.68, and parking is $25 a night. It also shows a $300 incidental deposit at check-in.

That produces $2,965.68 in actual stay charges: $2,514 room, $301.68 tax, and $150 parking. Breakfast adds no charge. The $300 incidental deposit is separate if it is a refundable authorization rather than a fee, so it should not be added to the trip total, though you need that much available at check-in.

The Omni quote says Premier Direct Ocean View King with Furnished Balcony. Room charge $2,346. Resort fee $49 per night, taxes $316.80, and self-parking is included in this package. They want $1,173 now and mention a $200 incidental hold at arrival.

The Omni's comparable stay total is $2,956.80: $2,346 room, $294 resort fee for six nights, and $316.80 tax. Included parking adds nothing. The $1,173 due now needs clarification because it may be an advance payment applied to the total rather than an extra charge. The $200 incidental hold is also outside the total if refundable.
It says the $1,173 is a two-night advance deposit credited against the room balance. The $200 is released after checkout if there are no charges.

Then neither amount increases the Omni total. You would pay $1,173 in advance and the remaining $1,783.80 under the hotel's payment schedule. Separately, the hotel would authorize $200 at arrival and release the unused amount afterward. The complete Omni cost remains $2,956.80.
So the Omni is only $8.88 less? I thought its room rate was much cheaper.

Correct. Its base room charge is $168 lower, but the $294 resort fee consumes most of that advantage. Elizabeth Pointe then adds $150 for parking. After all mandatory charges, Omni is $8.88 less: $2,956.80 versus $2,965.68.
Now verify what the balcony language actually guarantees. I do not want partial ocean view quietly turned into oceanfront, or the reverse.

Elizabeth Pointe guarantees a private balcony on a higher floor with a partial ocean view. That does not guarantee a straight-on Atlantic view; the ocean may be visible at an angle or across part of the property. Omni guarantees a furnished private balcony in the Premier Direct Ocean View category. Based on that exact category wording, the view is direct ocean-facing, but it should not be renamed oceanfront unless the hotel's confirmation itself uses that term.
Good. For this trip only, don't use walking distance to the beach as the deciding test. Both properties have direct beach access, so the guaranteed balcony view should carry more weight.
Understood. For this Amelia Island decision, beach proximity does not separate them; I will compare the guaranteed room view, complete cost, deposit timing, and cancellation exposure.

Elizabeth Pointe is free to cancel until 6:00 p.m. local time September 4. After that, it charges two nights. Omni is free through 11:59 p.m. local time September 5, and after that the two-night deposit is forfeited. Are those effectively the same penalty?

They are similar in size but not identical in timing or wording. Elizabeth Pointe's post-deadline penalty is two nights, and its deadline arrives September 4 at 6:00 p.m. Omni's $1,173 two-night advance deposit becomes nonrefundable after its later deadline, September 5 at 11:59 p.m. Before that deadline, the Omni deposit should be returned on cancellation. Omni therefore gives you about 30 additional hours to cancel without penalty.
Does the larger Omni deposit make it the worse option even though it comes back if we cancel in time?

It creates a cash-flow disadvantage, not a higher trip cost. Omni ties up $1,173 before arrival, while Elizabeth Pointe's quoted $300 is only an incidental authorization at check-in. The Omni deposit matters if you want to keep funds available or are concerned about refund-processing time. Financially, the greater risk begins only after September 5, when that deposit becomes the cancellation penalty.
Give me the stronger booking option, but state the reason without overselling an eight-dollar difference.

Omni is the stronger booking option. The meaningful advantage is the guaranteed Premier Direct Ocean View furnished balcony, compared with Elizabeth Pointe's partial-ocean-view balcony; the $8.88 savings is negligible. Omni also has the later cancellation deadline and included parking. Its drawback is the $1,173 advance deposit, even though that money is credited toward the $2,956.80 total and is refundable if you cancel by 11:59 p.m. local time September 5. Elizabeth Pointe remains the better cash-flow option because its $2,965.68 total requires no stated advance room deposit and only a refundable $300 incidental hold at arrival. Nothing has been booked.
